afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 252259
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
400 PM MST Wed Nov 25 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and tranquil weather will persist through at least the weekend 
as temperatures gradually warm into a slightly above normal range. 

- Periods of breezy conditions over high terrain areas and along the 
lower Colorado River Valley will be common through Thursday.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Dry and mostly tranquil weather conditions are expected to continue 
through the end of the week. As of early this afternoon, upper level 
water vapor satellite imagery shows a shortwave trough across 
southern CA and the Baja peninsula. The center can be seen just 
inland across south-central CA. This shortwave trough has tightened 
the pressure gradient across our area and has lead to some breezy 
conditions across SE CA and the higher terrain areas across AZ. This 
system will continue to progress south-southeastward, eventually 
becoming a closed low over the Baja peninsula tomorrow. While this 
system will mostly pass to our south it will lead to continued 
occasional breezy conditions across SE CA and the AZ higher terrain 
through at least tomorrow afternoon.

Ridging will begin to build back into Western CONUS on Thursday as 
the aforementioned closed low slowly progresses south-southeastward 
across Mexico. Temperatures will increase slightly tomorrow, as 
ridging builds back into the area, but then temperatures will remain 
fairly steady through the end of the week. Daily afternoon high 
temperatures will run 3-8 degrees above normal, with highs 
forecasted to be in the mid to upper 70s to right around 80 degrees 
across the lower deserts and range from the mid 60s to mid 70s 
across the higher terrain areas. Morning lows will generally be in 
the 40s to mid 50s across the area. The aforementioned shortwave is 
a dry system, and with the current dry air in place over the region, 
dry conditions will persist.

&&

.LONG TERM /SATURDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/... 
The upcoming weekend calls for the Pacific ridge to remain dominant 
across our region, but it will be in a weakening phase and is likely 
to get knocked down by a fast moving disturbance passing across the 
Four Corners area. Even with H5 heights dropping to between 580-
583dm, temperatures are not expected to drop much with lower desert 
highs at least maintaining mid 70s for highs. The weather pattern 
suggests another brief shortwave ridge moving through on Monday 
and/or Tuesday, but models are favoring a gradual increase in 
moisture early next week pushing PWAT anomalies to around 150-175% 
of normal by Tuesday. Temperatures are not expected to change much 
early next week despite the expected increase in clouds. Models then 
favor a more significant Pacific disturbance approaching the 
California coast and then likely passing through our region during 
the middle of next week. The timing, strength, and exact track of 
the system is still quite uncertain, but there are at least decent 
signs it will contain adequate moisture for some precipitation 
chances for our region. We expect it will be at least a few more 
days until we have a good idea on rain potential for next week's 
weather system.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2300Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Uncertainty and high variability in wind direction will be the main 
weather issues through Thursday evening as thick cirrus cigs 
gradually clear.  Confidence is good that an E/NE wind component 
will prevail the majority of the period, however, large variability 
will be possible. The typical cold season counter-intuitive light SW 
component experienced at KPHX the past few mornings may occur again 
early Thursday. There's a higher probability wind directions turn 
W/NW for a longer time frame late Thursday afternoon/evening than 
the past couple days. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No weather issues will exist through Thursday evening as high cirrus 
cigs give way to clear skies. Confidence is very good that winds 
will behave similarly to the past 24 hours, generally varying 
between a westerly and northerly trajectory. Extended periods of 
variability to nearly calm conditions will be common. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry and tranquil conditions will continue across the region. 
Temperatures will warm to above normal by Thursday region wide and 
remain around 3-8 degrees above normal through the weekend. MinRH's 
will range between 15-30% through most of the forecast period, while 
cool overnight lows will result in decent to good overnight recovery 
each night. Outside of periods of marginally breezy conditions over 
AZ high terrain areas and the Lower Colorado River Valley (mainly 
today through Thursday), light winds will be favored. Looking ahead, 
a weather system could move through the region during the middle of 
next week bringing some rain chances to portions of the area along 
with cooler temperatures and breezy to locally windy conditions. A 
lot of details are still uncertain at this time.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...Updated 11/25 2040Z. 
Gila River: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area due to continued water releases upwards of 
2500 cfs. Water levels near Dateland continue to rise, with gauge 
data now showing a depth of just above 7.5 ft and flow around 1250 
cfs. At the current rate of rise, the water level at the Dateland 
gauge is expected to reach action stage (8 ft) by Friday. A separate 
Flood Warning segment remains in effect from Dateland to Yuma. These 
water levels will have the potential to flood farm fields and low 
water crossings along the river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Berislavich
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...18
FIRE WEATHER...Berislavich 
HYDROLOGY...Berislavich/Benedict/RW
